Without it every test file emitted MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON: Node
parsed each one as CommonJS, failed, and reparsed it as ESM — roughly
seventy times per run, with the warning noting the cost each time. The
noise was the smaller half of the problem; a warning that always fires
is a warning nobody reads, and this one sat above every test result in
Node's own suggestion is to add "type": "module" to the package's
package.json, and that would break the application: the backend builds
to CommonJS in dist/ and the API loads it with require(). A nested
package.json scopes the declaration to this directory, because Node
resolves module type from the nearest one. dist/ is unaffected.
